title: Geography Lec 6
summary: Population rates 2011: CBR 21.8, CDR 7.1, IMR 44, U5MR 55 (per thousand).
Push factors (backwardness, insecurity) drive people out; pull factors (employment, peace) attract them.
Physiological density = total population / net cultivated area; India is in the third stage of the DTM.
Density 2011: Bihar 1106 (state), Delhi 11,320 (UT); lowest Arunachal Pradesh 17 and Andaman & Nicobar 46.
Sex ratio 943; Kerala 1084, Haryana 879, Puducherry 1037, Daman & Diu lowest.
Tribes: Bhil > Gond > Santhal; India has 8 major industrial regions; Class I city = 1 lakh or more.
Golden Quadrilateral 5,846 km (1999-2012), NH-44 longest; NS and EW corridors meet at Jhansi.
NW-1 Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly is the longest; Suez Canal 1869, 193 km; Trans-Siberian ~9,300 km, 8 time zones.
Railway zone HQs: NW Jaipur, WC Jabalpur, EC Hajipur, NC Prayagraj, SECR Bilaspur, NE Gorakhpur.
DVC 1948, TVA model, four dams; Kudremukh magnetite iron ore; four iron ore belts.
Coal: anthracite highest grade, peat lowest; lignite = brown coal (Neyveli); bituminous most common; Gondwana coal dominant.
Lakes: Wular largest freshwater, Chilika largest lagoon, Sambhar inland saline, Vembanad longest, Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar largest artificial.
18 biosphere reserves; Jim Corbett first national park (1936), Project Tiger 1973; Similipal Odisha's second national park (2025).
Atmosphere: weather occurs in the troposphere (13 km avg); ozone in the stratosphere; mesosphere coldest; ionosphere reflects radio waves.

mcqs.q: What was India's crude birth rate (per thousand population) in 2011, approximately?
mcqs.e: CBR = (live births / mid-year population) x 1000; 21.8 in 2011.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct formula for crude birth rate (B = live births, P = mid-year population)?
mcqs.e: CBR is the number of births per 1000 population.

mcqs.q: What was India's crude death rate (per thousand) in 2011?
mcqs.e: CDR in 2011 = 7.1 per thousand.

mcqs.q: What was India's infant mortality rate (IMR) in 2011, approximately?
mcqs.e: IMR = deaths of infants under one year per thousand live births.

mcqs.q: What was India's under-five mortality rate (per thousand live births) in 2011, approximately?
Which of the following is NOT a 'pull factor' of migration?
mcqs.e: Backwardness is a push factor; employment, peace and security are pull factors.

mcqs.q: What does a 'push factor' mean in migration?
o: A factor that attracts people to a new place
Migration caused only by government schemes
A factor that compels people to leave their place of origin
Migration linked only to seasonal pastoralism
mcqs.e: Push = unemployment, violence, backwardness; pull = employment, peace.

mcqs.q: Which density measures the pressure of population on the net cultivated area in India?
mcqs.e: Physiological density = total population / net cultivated area.

mcqs.q: What is the denominator in the calculation of physiological density?
mcqs.e: Arithmetic density uses total area; this uses only the net sown area.

mcqs.q: How do extremely dense 'mega regions' like Tokyo-Osaka and the Pearl River Delta develop?
o: Through forced settlement by the government
Through integrated economic corridors and high connectivity
mcqs.e: Dubai too grew from desert into a mega region thanks to its ports and airports.

mcqs.q: A country with a high birth rate and a high death rate is in which stage of the Demographic Transition Model (DTM)?
mcqs.e: In the first stage both rates are high and population stays nearly stable.

mcqs.q: In which stage of the DTM does a population explosion occur?
o: Second - birth rate high, death rate falls rapidly
mcqs.e: Better healthcare lowers the death rate while the birth rate stays high.

mcqs.q: What is the characteristic of the fourth stage of the DTM?
o: High birth rate, low death rate
Both birth and death rates low
Low birth rate, high death rate
mcqs.e: Seen in developed economies; India is in the third stage.

mcqs.q: What is the full form of 'DINK', which describes the trend of fewer children in urban families?
mcqs.e: Rising female literacy lowers the birth rate.

mcqs.q: Which factor has the most direct influence on the location and growth of human settlements?
mcqs.e: Water scarcity keeps the Rajasthan desert sparse; water and fertile soil make the Ganga plain dense.

mcqs.q: Which combination contributes to low population density?
o: Flat land, fertile soil, urban jobs
Harsh climate, poor soil, few roads
mcqs.e: Flat, fertile, well-watered areas with jobs are densely settled.

mcqs.q: What is the main feature of Brazil's demographic change since the 1980s?
o: Rise in birth rate, fall in death rate
Fall in both birth and death rates
mcqs.e: Brazil is shifting from a young to an ageing population.

mcqs.q: Which industrial region of India is the most prominent port-based one?
mcqs.e: The Hugli region has the Kolkata and Haldia ports.

mcqs.q: How many major industrial regions are recognised in India?
mcqs.e: Mumbai-Pune, Bengaluru-TN, Gujarat, Chota Nagpur, Visakhapatnam-Guntur, Gurugram-Delhi-Meerut, Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram, Hugli.

mcqs.q: The Chota Nagpur industrial region is famous for what?
o: Minerals like coal and iron ore
mcqs.e: A region of mineral-based heavy industries.

mcqs.q: The Visakhapatnam-Guntur industrial region is known for what?
mcqs.e: A region in Andhra Pradesh.

mcqs.q: The Gujarat industrial region is famous for which industries?
mcqs.e: Surat is a major diamond-processing centre.

mcqs.q: The Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram industrial region is mainly known for what?
mcqs.e: An industrial region of Kerala.

mcqs.q: The Bengaluru-Tamil Nadu industrial region is known for what?
mcqs.e: A major industrial region of South India.

mcqs.q: As per Census 2011, which Indian state has the highest population density?
mcqs.e: Bihar 1,106 persons/sq km; West Bengal second (1,028).

mcqs.q: As per Census 2011, which Union Territory has the highest population density?
mcqs.e: Delhi 11,320 persons/sq km.

mcqs.q: As per Census 2011, which Union Territory has the lowest population density?
mcqs.e: The density of A&N Islands is about 46.

mcqs.q: Which Indian state has the lowest population density?
mcqs.e: Arunachal Pradesh has about 17 persons per sq km.

mcqs.q: As per Census 2011, which Union Territory has the highest sex ratio?
mcqs.e: Among states, Kerala is highest (1084).

mcqs.q: Which country had the lowest median age (youngest country) in 2024?
mcqs.e: Niger's median age is about 15 years.

mcqs.q: According to UN projections, which region will contribute most to global population growth up to 2050?
mcqs.e: Nigeria, Ethiopia, Kenya, DR Congo and others.

mcqs.q: What does a very broad base of a population pyramid indicate?
o: More children; population will grow rapidly in future
mcqs.e: Broad base = high birth rate, young population.

mcqs.q: What does a rectangular population pyramid indicate?
mcqs.e: A pyramid narrowing at the base (bell-shaped) shows a declining population.

mcqs.q: A population pyramid with a narrow base and a wide top indicates what?
o: Low birth rate and low life expectancy
Low birth rate and high life expectancy
High birth rate and high death rate
High birth rate and low death rate
mcqs.e: Seen in developed countries like Japan.

mcqs.q: The Gond tribe is mainly found in which state?
mcqs.e: The Gonds are a tribe of central India (Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh).

mcqs.q: Which is the largest tribe of India?
mcqs.e: Order: Bhil, Gond, Santhal.

mcqs.q: Which is the second largest tribe of India?
mcqs.e: Order: Bhil, Gond, Santhal.

mcqs.q: Which is the third largest tribe of India?
mcqs.e: Santhals live in Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha.

mcqs.q: The Konyak tribe is mainly found in which state?
mcqs.e: The Konyaks are a Naga tribe.

mcqs.q: What is the most common type of rural settlement in the northern plains (UP, Bihar)?
mcqs.e: Dense population leads to compact villages.

mcqs.q: When small groups of houses such as 'purwa/tola' together form a village, it is called a:
mcqs.e: The village is split into several small units.

mcqs.q: Which factor most influences dispersed settlements in hilly and forested areas?
mcqs.e: In Himachal and Uttarakhand houses lie far apart.

mcqs.q: Why can the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) sometimes exceed 100%?
o: The numerator also counts students outside the official age group
mcqs.e: GER = (total enrolment / population of official age group) x 100.

mcqs.q: What was India's decadal population growth rate during 2001-2011, approximately?
mcqs.e: Decadal growth was 17.64%.

mcqs.q: What was India's annual population growth rate during 2001-2011, approximately?
mcqs.e: Annual growth was 1.64%.

mcqs.q: Which state recorded the highest population growth rate during 2001-11?
mcqs.e: About 28%.

mcqs.q: Which Union Territory recorded the highest population growth during 2001-11?
mcqs.e: Due to industry-driven in-migration.

mcqs.q: What is India's sex ratio (2011)?
mcqs.e: Highest Kerala (1084), lowest Haryana (879).

mcqs.q: Which state had the lowest sex ratio in 2011?
mcqs.e: Among UTs, Daman and Diu is lowest.

mcqs.q: Which Union Territory had the lowest sex ratio in 2011?
mcqs.e: Highest among UTs: Puducherry.

mcqs.q: As per Census 2011, which urban agglomeration has the largest population?
mcqs.e: Delhi is densest, but Greater Mumbai leads in total population, followed by Delhi.

mcqs.q: What type of city is Kanpur (UP)?
mcqs.e: Famous for textile and leather industries.

mcqs.q: In the 2011 Census, which town is called a 'Class I' city?
o: One with a population of 1 lakh or more

mcqs.q: In the Indian context, population growth of Class I cities is mainly driven by:
mcqs.e: Population changes through births, deaths and migration.

mcqs.q: In India, a town with a population of 5,000 to 10,000 falls in which class?
mcqs.e: Class VI is below 5,000.

mcqs.q: Which was the phase of steady population growth in India?
mcqs.e: 1901-21 stagnant, 1921-51 steady, 1951-81 explosion, post-1981 slowdown.

mcqs.q: Which year is called the 'Year of the Great Divide' in India's demographic history?
mcqs.e: After 1921, population began to grow continuously.

mcqs.q: Which was the period of population explosion in India?
mcqs.e: Mortality fell rapidly while fertility stayed high.

mcqs.q: What is the main cause of rapid population growth in the second stage of the DTM?
o: High birth rate and falling death rate
mcqs.e: Improved medical facilities reduce the death rate.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an inland riverine port?
mcqs.e: Pandu is at Guwahati on the Brahmaputra.

mcqs.q: What type of port is Kolkata port?
mcqs.e: Now called Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port.

mcqs.q: What type of port is Kandla, and what is its new name?
mcqs.e: Water level changes with the tides.

mcqs.q: What is special about Visakhapatnam port?
mcqs.e: It is not a riverine port.

mcqs.q: By what nickname is Kochi known?
mcqs.e: A major port of Kerala.

mcqs.q: How many major ports does India have?
mcqs.e: 12 major ports, of which Kamarajar (Ennore), Tamil Nadu, is run as a company.

mcqs.q: Which is India's first corporatised major port (registered as a company)?
mcqs.e: Located in Tamil Nadu; it is government-owned, not private.

mcqs.q: Which port at the Zuari estuary was remodelled in 1961 to export iron ore to Japan?
mcqs.e: A port in Goa.

mcqs.q: Most of the route of the Orient Express lies in which continent?
mcqs.e: From Paris (France) to Istanbul (Turkey); started in 1883.

mcqs.q: The Orient Express originally connected which cities?
mcqs.e: A trans-continental route started in 1883.

mcqs.q: The Golden Quadrilateral connects which cities?
mcqs.e: Total length 5,846 km.

mcqs.q: The Golden Quadrilateral project was launched during whose tenure?
mcqs.e: Started in 1999, completed in 2012.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest segment of the Golden Quadrilateral?
mcqs.e: This segment runs along NH-16.

mcqs.q: Which is the shortest segment of the Golden Quadrilateral?
mcqs.e: This segment runs along NH-48.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest National Highway in India?
mcqs.e: Runs from Jammu & Kashmir to Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.q: At which place do the North-South and East-West corridors intersect?
mcqs.e: NS: Srinagar-Kanyakumari (about 4,000 km).

mcqs.q: The East-West corridor connects which two places?
mcqs.e: About 3,300 km long.

mcqs.q: What is the meeting point of two or more transport routes called?
mcqs.e: A grid is a specific network structure.

mcqs.q: On which National Waterway is the floating terminal at Farakka located?
mcqs.e: NW-1: Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly (Prayagraj-Haldia), the longest waterway.

mcqs.q: National Waterway-2 is on which river?
mcqs.e: Dhubri-Sadiya in Assam.

mcqs.q: National Waterway-3 lies between which places?
mcqs.e: West Coast Canal; NW-4 Kakinada region (AP), NW-5 Odisha-West Bengal.

mcqs.q: Which waterway connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea?
mcqs.e: A man-made canal controlled by Egypt.

mcqs.q: In which year was the Suez Canal formally opened?
mcqs.e: Built 1859-1869; length about 193 km.

mcqs.q: The Strait of Hormuz connects:
o: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
Gulf of Oman and Persian Gulf
mcqs.e: Vital for oil exports from the Persian Gulf.

mcqs.q: Which strait is called the 'Gate of Tears'?
mcqs.e: Connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.

mcqs.q: Which navigator reached India via the Cape of Good Hope?
mcqs.e: The Suez Canal is a shorter alternative to this route.

mcqs.q: The Trans-Siberian Railway connects which cities?
mcqs.e: The world's longest railway line.

mcqs.q: What is the approximate length of the Trans-Siberian Railway?
mcqs.e: It spans eight time zones in Russia.

mcqs.q: Why is air transport less popular for freight in India?
o: It is costly; suitable only for light, high-value goods
mcqs.e: Fuel cost is high for heavy cargo.

mcqs.q: In which century did railway development begin in India?
mcqs.e: First train Bombay to Thane, 1853, under Lord Dalhousie.

mcqs.q: The HBJ pipeline is used to transport what?
mcqs.e: Operated by GAIL (Gas Authority of India Limited).

mcqs.q: The HBJ pipeline connects which states?
mcqs.e: Hazira (Gujarat), Bijaipur (MP), Jagdishpur (UP).

mcqs.q: Where is the headquarters of the North Western Railway zone?
mcqs.e: Hajipur - East Central; Hubballi - South Western; New Delhi - Northern.

mcqs.q: Where is the headquarters of East Central Railway?
mcqs.e: West Central - Jabalpur; East Central - Hajipur.

mcqs.q: Where is the headquarters of West Central Railway?
mcqs.e: North Central - Prayagraj; South Central - Secunderabad.

mcqs.q: Where is the headquarters of North Eastern Railway?
mcqs.e: Northeast Frontier Railway - Maligaon (Guwahati).

mcqs.q: Where is the headquarters of South East Central Railway?
mcqs.e: East Coast - Bhubaneswar; South Coast - Visakhapatnam; South Eastern - Kolkata.

mcqs.q: The headquarters of the Northern, Southern, Eastern and Western Railway zones are respectively at:
mcqs.e: HQs of the original four zones.

mcqs.q: The Pamban bridge/island is in which state?
mcqs.e: Connects Rameswaram island to the mainland.

mcqs.q: What is a major challenge for developing inland waterways in India?
mcqs.e: High private investment is not a challenge.

mcqs.q: What is the main reason for higher road density in Kerala compared to Rajasthan?
mcqs.e: Rajasthan has low population density and less suitable terrain.

mcqs.q: Which mineral has abundant reserves in the Damodar Valley?
mcqs.e: DVC was established in 1948.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC) is correct?
o: Established in 1948; India's first multipurpose project
mcqs.e: Nehru called dams the 'temples of modern India'.

mcqs.q: The Damodar Valley Project was modelled on which foreign project?
mcqs.e: TVA was a project in the USA.

mcqs.q: Which of the following dams was NOT built under the DVC?
mcqs.e: DVC: Tilaiya, Konar, Maithon, Panchet; Hirakud is on the Mahanadi.

mcqs.q: Kudremukh (Karnataka) is famous for which mineral?
mcqs.e: Kudre = horse, mukh = face; part of the Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt.

mcqs.q: Which region of Maharashtra is known for iron ore?
mcqs.e: India has four iron ore belts.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a non-metallic natural resource?
mcqs.e: Limestone/dolomite gives rise to karst topography.

mcqs.q: Kolar Gold Fields (KGF) and Hutti gold mines are in which state?
mcqs.e: KGF is now closed.

mcqs.q: Which plateau region is rich in both iron ore and coal?
mcqs.e: North-eastern peninsular plateau.

mcqs.q: Jhunjhunu and Alwar districts are known for the production of which mineral?
mcqs.e: The Khetri mines (Jhunjhunu) are famous.

mcqs.q: Which ore of copper begins with the letter 'M'?
mcqs.e: Copper is considered the first metal used by humans.

mcqs.q: Mica is used in the electrical industry because of which property?
o: High dielectric strength; poor conductor of heat and electricity
mcqs.e: A non-metallic mineral, also used in cosmetics.

mcqs.q: Which state ranks first in mica production in India?
mcqs.e: Andhra Pradesh (Nellore) leads, followed by Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Which state has the largest bauxite reserves in India?
mcqs.e: The Panchpatmali mines (Odisha) are famous.

mcqs.q: What is the main reason for the decline of high-grade ores in India in recent decades?
mcqs.e: Only the rich ores were exploited.

mcqs.q: Where are manganese nodules mainly found?
mcqs.e: They are also called polymetallic nodules.

mcqs.q: What is the objective of the 'Samudrayaan Mission'?
mcqs.e: Matsya-6000: titanium submersible, 3 crew, 6,000 m depth.

mcqs.q: Which institution is developing the Matsya-6000 submersible?
mcqs.e: National Institute of Ocean Technology.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest iron ore producing state in India?
mcqs.e: Keonjhar, Mayurbhanj, Sundargarh, Badampahar.

mcqs.q: The Bailadila iron ore mines are in which state?
mcqs.e: Jharkhand has Singhbhum and Noamundi.

mcqs.q: Which type of coal is known as 'brown coal'?
mcqs.e: The main source of lignite is Neyveli (Tamil Nadu).

mcqs.q: Which is the highest grade of coal?
mcqs.e: High carbon, low moisture; order: peat < lignite < bituminous < anthracite.

mcqs.q: Which is the lowest grade of coal?
mcqs.e: Peat has the highest moisture content.

mcqs.q: Which coal is found most abundantly in India?
mcqs.e: Used as metallurgical coal.

mcqs.q: Where is Tertiary coal found in India?
mcqs.e: Most of India's coal is Gondwana coal.

mcqs.q: Why is coal called 'buried sunshine'?
o: It forms from the sun's heat
It is matter fallen from the sun
It is formed from fossils of ancient plants
mcqs.e: Fossils turn into coal under great pressure and heat; a non-renewable resource.

mcqs.q: Which of the following energy sources is non-renewable?
mcqs.e: Coal is not formed at the rate at which it is consumed.

mcqs.q: Which industry is set up near the source of raw material (heavy industry)?
mcqs.e: Because the raw materials are heavy.

mcqs.q: Which three steel plants were set up during the Second Five-Year Plan?
mcqs.e: Rourkela (Odisha), Durgapur (WB), Bhilai (Chhattisgarh).

mcqs.q: What is meant by a footloose industry?
o: Not tied to raw-material sources; can be set up anywhere
mcqs.e: Example: diamonds - mined at Panna, processed at Surat.

mcqs.q: The Sardar Sarovar Project is on which river?
mcqs.e: The Indira Sagar Dam is also on the Narmada.

mcqs.q: Which Indian river crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice?
mcqs.e: The Mahi drains into the Gulf of Khambhat.

mcqs.q: Jawahar Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar and Gandhi Sagar dams are on which river?
mcqs.e: Gandhi Sagar is in MP; the other two are in Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: The Ukai Dam is on which river?
mcqs.e: Located in Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest gravity dam in India?
mcqs.e: Bhakra is in Himachal Pradesh and Nangal in Punjab.

mcqs.q: Which is the highest dam in India?
mcqs.e: Tehri is an earth-and-rockfill dam in Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest dam in India?
mcqs.e: Located at Sambalpur, Odisha.

mcqs.q: What was the ancient name of the Sutlej river?
mcqs.e: Rises at Rakshastal, enters India at Shipki La; called Langchen Khambab in Tibet.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest tributary of the Indus?
mcqs.e: The largest tributary (by volume) is the Chenab.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?
mcqs.e: Wular is fed by the Jhelum; Loktak is the largest in the North-east.

mcqs.q: By what name is Dal Lake known?
mcqs.e: Called the 'Jewel of Srinagar'.

mcqs.q: Loktak Lake is in which state?
mcqs.e: Home to Keibul Lamjao National Park; listed in the Montreux Record.

mcqs.q: Which is the world's only floating national park?
mcqs.e: On Loktak Lake in Manipur.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest brackish water lake in India?
mcqs.e: A coastal lagoon in Odisha.

mcqs.q: Chilika Lake spreads across which three districts of Odisha?
mcqs.e: India's largest coastal lagoon.

mcqs.q: Mizoram is also known by which name?
mcqs.e: It has the Dampa Tiger Reserve.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest inland saline lake in India?
mcqs.e: Located in Rajasthan; Chilika is a coastal lagoon.

mcqs.q: Pushkar Lake is in which district?
mcqs.e: Ana Sagar is also in Ajmer.

mcqs.q: Asia's largest oxbow lake (Kabar Tal) is in which state?
mcqs.e: In Begusarai district.

mcqs.q: Where is Pulicat Lake located?
mcqs.e: Second largest brackish coastal lagoon after Chilika.

mcqs.q: Which is the longest lake in India and where is it?
mcqs.e: Kerala's backwaters are called 'kayals'.

mcqs.q: The Nehru Trophy Boat Race is held on which kayal?
mcqs.e: At Alappuzha.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Kolleru Lake is correct?
o: Not a lagoon but a freshwater lake between the Godavari and Krishna in Andhra Pradesh
mcqs.e: Pulicat, Chilika and Vembanad are lagoons.

mcqs.q: What type of lake is Lonar Lake?
o: Crater lake formed by a meteorite impact
mcqs.e: In Buldhana district, Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: The Koyna project is built on a tributary of which river?
mcqs.e: Krishna tributaries: Bhima, Tungabhadra, Musi, Koyna, Ghataprabha, Malaprabha, Dudhganga.

mcqs.q: Where are Pangong Tso and Tso Moriri lakes located?
mcqs.e: Both are saltwater lakes.

mcqs.q: Gurudongmar Lake is in which state?
mcqs.e: One of the highest-altitude lakes in India.

mcqs.q: From where does the Indira Gandhi Canal originate?
mcqs.e: Irrigates the Rajasthan desert.

mcqs.q: Where does the Chambal river rise and of which river is it a tributary?
mcqs.e: Famous for its ravine (badland) topography.

mcqs.q: The Tehri Dam is on which river?
mcqs.e: India's highest dam.

mcqs.q: At which prayag do the Bhagirathi and Alaknanda meet?
mcqs.e: From here onwards the river is called the Ganga.

mcqs.q: Where does the Mandakini river join the Alaknanda?
mcqs.e: Pindar-Karnaprayag; Nandakini-Nandprayag; Dhauliganga-Vishnuprayag.

mcqs.q: Where does the Pindar river join the Alaknanda?
mcqs.e: One of the Panch Prayag.

mcqs.q: By what name is Barapani Lake near Shillong known?
mcqs.e: Located in Meghalaya.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest artificial lake in India?
mcqs.e: On the Rihand (a Son tributary) in UP; named after UP's first Chief Minister.

mcqs.q: Jaisamand (Dhebar) Lake, one of the largest artificial lakes in India, is in which district?
mcqs.e: Located in Rajasthan.

mcqs.q: Which is the largest brackish water wetland in India overall?
mcqs.e: Largest inland saline wetland: Sambhar.

mcqs.q: Which lake of Rajasthan is artificial?
mcqs.e: Built by Arnoraja (grandfather of Prithviraj Chauhan) in 1135-1150.

mcqs.q: Pitti Island of Lakshadweep is known for what?
mcqs.e: No permanent residents live there.

mcqs.q: The Desert National Park of Rajasthan lies in which districts?
mcqs.e: Famous for the Great Indian Bustard (Godawan).

mcqs.q: The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve is in which state?
mcqs.e: World's largest mangrove forest; famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger.

mcqs.q: Which was India's first biosphere reserve?
mcqs.e: Got UNESCO recognition in 2000; spread over Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka.

mcqs.q: How many biosphere reserves are there in India?
mcqs.e: Many of them are in UNESCO's MAB network.

mcqs.q: The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve is in which state?
mcqs.e: Added to UNESCO's MAB network in 2025.

mcqs.q: In which state is Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve and by what nickname is it known?
o: Maharashtra; Queen of the Western Ghats
mcqs.e: Located in the Satpura Range.

mcqs.q: In which state is Similipal, and what was it declared in April 2025?
mcqs.e: Odisha's first national park is Bhitarkanika.

mcqs.q: The Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve lies on the border of which states?
mcqs.e: Amarkantak is the source of the Narmada.

mcqs.q: Where is Khangchendzonga located and what is its distinction?
o: Sikkim; India's only mixed World Heritage Site
mcqs.e: Inscribed on both natural and cultural criteria.

mcqs.q: Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is in which state?
mcqs.e: Nanda Devi is in Uttarakhand.

mcqs.q: The Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve is in which Union Territory?
mcqs.e: Gulf of Mannar is in Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.q: Kaziranga National Park is famous for what?
mcqs.e: Located in Assam.

mcqs.q: Ranthambore National Park is in which state?
mcqs.e: Famous for tigers.

mcqs.q: Which statement about Jim Corbett National Park is correct?
o: India's first national park (1936), in Uttarakhand; Project Tiger began here
India's second national park, in Rajasthan
mcqs.e: Formerly called Hailey National Park.

mcqs.q: In which year was Project Tiger launched?
mcqs.e: It began at Jim Corbett.

mcqs.q: The Valley of Flowers and Rajaji National Park are in which state?
mcqs.e: Rajaji was in the news recently for its wildlife corridor.

mcqs.q: Silent Valley National Park is in which state?
mcqs.e: In Palakkad district.

mcqs.q: Orang, Manas and Dibru-Saikhowa National Parks are in which state?
mcqs.e: Buxa Tiger Reserve is in West Bengal.

mcqs.q: Bhitarkanika National Park is in which state?
mcqs.e: Known for mangroves and saltwater crocodiles.

mcqs.q: Pench National Park lies on the border of which states?
mcqs.e: Night safari has been permitted here.

mcqs.q: Kanha, Madhav and Bandhavgarh National Parks are in which state?
mcqs.e: MP has the most national parks.

mcqs.q: Dudhwa National Park is in which state?
mcqs.e: In Lakhimpur Kheri district.

mcqs.q: In which park have cheetahs been reintroduced in India?
mcqs.e: In Sheopur district, MP.

mcqs.q: Gir National Park is famous for what?
mcqs.e: In Gujarat; Vansda National Park is also in Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Which is the lowest layer of the atmosphere?
mcqs.e: All weather phenomena occur here.

mcqs.q: What is the average height of the troposphere?
mcqs.e: About 18 km at the equator and 8 km at the poles.

mcqs.q: Why is the troposphere higher over the equator?
o: Intense heating carries convection currents higher
mcqs.e: Convection is weaker at the poles.

mcqs.q: What is the rate at which temperature decreases with height (normal lapse rate)?
mcqs.e: About 1 degree per 165 metres.

mcqs.q: In which layer of the atmosphere is the ozone layer found?
mcqs.e: It protects against harmful UV rays; the stratosphere extends up to about 50 km.

mcqs.q: When and why is International Ozone Day observed?
o: 16 September - signing of the Montreal Protocol in 1987
mcqs.e: For controlling CFCs; ozone thickness is measured in Dobson units.

mcqs.q: Which is the coldest layer of the atmosphere?
mcqs.e: Extends up to about 85 km; meteors burn up here.

mcqs.q: Which layer of the atmosphere reflects radio waves?
mcqs.e: It contains ions and temperature rises with height here.

mcqs.q: Which is the outermost layer of the atmosphere?
mcqs.e: Order: tropo-, strato-, meso-, thermo/iono-, exosphere.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order (percentage) of nitrogen, oxygen, argon and CO2 in the atmosphere?
mcqs.e: Standard textbook values.

mcqs.q: In which layer of the atmosphere do jet aircraft generally fly?
mcqs.e: It is free of clouds and weather disturbances.

mcqs.q: When does a spring tide occur?
o: When the Sun, Earth and Moon are in a straight line
mcqs.e: Neap tide occurs at 90 degrees, with a smaller tidal range.

mcqs.q: What happens in a semi-diurnal tide?
o: One high and one low tide
Two high and two low tides in about 24 hours 50 minutes
mcqs.e: A diurnal tide has one high and one low tide.
